items.stem: What permission level should a new tool connection start from?

options.text: Least privilege: only the access the task actually needs
options.rationale: Correct: least privilege limits the damage of any mistake or breach.
Broad access widens risk far beyond the task.

options.text: Whatever the default happens to be
options.rationale: Defaults may grant more than the task needs.

options.text: Write access to every system it can reach
options.rationale: Unneeded write access is a serious liability.

items.explanation: Correct: least privilege limits the damage of any mistake or breach.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO controls govern enterprise tool connections well? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Rotate tokens and audit the actions connections take
options.rationale: Correct: rotation and auditing limit and surface misuse.

options.text: Require approval before a new connection is added
options.rationale: Correct: an approval step prevents ungoverned connections.

options.text: Share one personal token across the whole team
options.rationale: Shared personal tokens defeat auditing and rotation.
Stale connections are an unnecessary attack surface.

items.explanation: Correct: rotation and auditing limit and surface misuse.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: After an agent completes a task using a connected tool, what should you do?

options.text: Audit the actions the tool actually performed
options.rationale: Correct: reviewing effects catches unintended actions.

options.text: Assume it did exactly what was asked
options.rationale: Unreviewed tool actions can have side effects.
Widening access without need increases risk.

options.text: Delete the task history to save space
options.rationale: History is what lets you audit what happened.

items.explanation: Correct: reviewing effects catches unintended actions.
